title: Why a write to the fleet cache did not end up stored, as a code, whether to try again and whether other machines would hit the same wall
description: Every write of the graph exchange ends in a stored entry or in exactly one refusal. A refusal comes from the answer of the cache (HTTP status and the first words of its body), from the client (no answer in time, no connection, the breaker of the machine is open) or from the limits the client checks before it sends anything. `transient` says that the same bytes may be accepted later (the caller keeps the finished work and tries again with a back-off); `deterministic` says that every machine would meet the same refusal (the caller writes a failure note so that the others stop inferring the owner); `stored` says that the cache already holds an entry for the key, so the work is not lost and not repeated. The rows are evaluated in order, the first row that matches wins.
